source_text:
Tractatus contra eos qui imagines faciunt
Λόγος τοῦ ἁγίου ̓Επιφανίου κατὰ τῶν ἐπιτηδευόντων ποιεῖν εἰδωλικῷ
θεσμῷ εἰκόνας εἰς ἀφομοίωσιν τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τῆς Θεοτόκου καὶ τῶν
μαρτύρων, ετι δὲ καὶ ἀγγέλων καὶ προφητῶν.
1 τὸν τοῖχον κονιάσαντες χρώμασι διηλλαγμένοις τὰς εἰκόνας ἀνετύπωσαν.
2 οτι δή, φασί, τὰς εἰκόνας τῶν ἁγίων ποιοῦμεν εἰς μνημόσυνον καὶ τιμὴν αὐτῶν. 3
ψευδωνύμους 4 πόθεν δὲ αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τῆς τοῦ ἀρχαγγέλλου γραφῆς οστεα καὶ νεῦρα
ἐνηρμοσμένα κατάδηλα ἐγένετο, τῆς ἐκείνου ην λέγειν συνέσεως. 5 οἱ νομίζοντες ἐν
τούτῳ τιμᾶν τοὺς ἀποστόλους, μαθέτωσαν οτι ἀντὶ τοῦ τιμᾶν, πλέον αὐτοὺς
ἀτιμάζουσιν.
Παῦλος γὰρ τὸν ψευδώνυμον ἱερέα ἐνυβρίσας τοῖχον κεκονιαμένον
ἀπεφήνατο.
orientation: Epiphanius opens his treatise by stating his target: those who make painted images of Christ, the Mother of God, martyrs, angels, and prophets, and he begins to answer their claim that the images are for memorial and honor.
pass_a_gloss: Discourse of the holy Epiphanius against those who practice making by an idolatrous custom images for images of Christ and of the Mother of God and of the martyrs, and further also of angels and prophets. Having whitewashed the wall with varied colors they impressed the images. Because, they say, we make the images of the saints for memorial and honor of them. the falsely named one. But whence to him, in the depiction of the archangel, bones and sinews fitted together became clearly visible, was of that one's understanding to say. Those who think by this to honor the apostles, let them learn that instead of honoring, they dishonor them more. For Paul, having insulted the falsely named priest, declared him a whitewashed wall.

choices.why: The glossary fixes this rendering for the phrase describing the practice Epiphanius opposes.
The glossary requires 'images' for the painted likenesses, avoiding the banned 'icons'.
The glossary fixes 'Mother of God' as the rendering for the title of Mary.
The glossary requires 'memorial' for the stated purpose of the images.
The glossary fixes 'falsely named' for this term, applied both to the opponents' claim and to the high priest.
Renders the purpose of the images as a making similar or assimilating, keeping the sense of representation.

pass_b_english: A discourse of Saint Epiphanius against those who make a practice of producing images according to an idolatrous custom, in likeness of Christ and of the Mother of God and of the martyrs, and further of angels and prophets.
They whitewashed the wall and impressed images on it with varied colors.
Because, they say, we make images of the saints as a memorial and for their honor.
But how did bones and sinews fitted together become visible to him in the painting of the archangel? It would take his own wit to say.
Those who think they honor the apostles in this way should learn that instead of honoring them, they dishonor them all the more.
For Paul, insulting the falsely named priest, declared him to be a whitewashed wall.
notes: The text at the start of section 3 appears damaged or truncated: 'ψευδωνύμους' stands alone, and section 4 begins mid-sentence with 'πόθεν δὲ αὐτῷ...', suggesting missing text or a corrupt transition. The gloss renders only what is present.

problems.quote: For Paul, insulting the falsely named priest, declared him to be a whitewashed wall (Acts 23:3).
problems.source_quote: Παῦλος γὰρ τὸν ψευδώνυμον ἱερέα ἐνυβρίσας τοῖχον κεκονιαμένον ἀπεφήνατο
problems.why: English adds '(Acts 23:3)' which is not in source. This is addition of scriptural reference.
problems.fix: For Paul, insulting the falsely named priest, declared him to be a whitewashed wall.
problems.ruling: Source has no Acts 23:3 reference; adding it misrepresents the Greek text to readers.

edits.old: For Paul, insulting the falsely named priest, declared him to be a whitewashed wall (Acts 23:3).
edits.new: For Paul, insulting the falsely named priest, declared him to be a whitewashed wall.

problems.quote: But how did bones and sinews fitted together become visible to him in the painting of the archangel? That belonged to the understanding of the one who says it.
problems.source_quote: πόθεν δὲ αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τῆς τοῦ ἀρχαγγέλλου γραφῆς ὀστέα καὶ νεῦρα ἐνηρμοσμένα κατάδηλα ἐγένετο, τῆς ἐκείνου ἦν λέγειν συνέσεως
problems.why: 'understanding of the one who says it' mistranslates τῆς ἐκείνου ἦν λέγειν συνέσεως. Means 'it was for him to say' or 'he had the wit to say it'—i.e., the painter used his own imagination. 'Belonged to the understanding' is obscure and wrong.
problems.fix: How did bones and fitted sinews become visible to him in the archangel's picture? That took his own fancy to invent.

edits.old: But how did bones and sinews fitted together become visible to him in the painting of the archangel? That belonged to the understanding of the one who says it.
edits.new: But how did bones and sinews fitted together become visible to him in the painting of the archangel? That took his own fancy to invent.

problems.quote: That took his own fancy to invent
problems.why: 'fancy to invent' adds notion of invention not in Greek; 'λέγειν' is 'to say/speak,' not 'invent.' The phrase means 'it was for his own wisdom to say' or 'that was his own wisdom speaking'—mocking the painter's supposed knowledge.
problems.fix: That was his own wisdom speaking

edits.old: That took his own fancy to invent.
edits.new: That was his own wisdom speaking.

fixed: The other two edits already tried were not confirmed problems; the English already matches the source for those passages.

problems.why: Same Greek concept (pseudōnymos) appears as adjective and noun phrase; reader may miss Paul's target is same person.

problems.quote: That was his own wisdom speaking.
problems.why: Unclear who 'his' refers to; the painter? the archangel? Paul? No antecedent established.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'That was the painter's own fancy speaking.'

problems.quote: impressed images on it with varied colors
problems.why: 'Impressed' suggests stamping or pressing; painters apply color, they do not impress it. Greek may mean 'daubed' or 'painted over'.

problems.quote: They whitewashed the wall and impressed images on it with varied colors. Because, they say, we make images of the saints as a memorial and for their honor. Falsely named.
problems.why: Three disconnected sentences with no logical connector; 'Falsely named' hangs without subject, appearing to modify the preceding clause about memorials.
problems.fix: Reconstruct syntax: 'They are falsely named who say...'

problems.why: Ambiguous whether this labels the practice, the priest, or is a standalone comment.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'This is falsely named' or 'He is falsely named a priest.'

problems.quote: those who make a practice of producing images
problems.why: The opponents are described variously, possibly suggesting different groups.

variants.text: those who make a practice of producing images

edits.old: They whitewashed the wall and impressed images on it with varied colors.
edits.new: They whitewashed the wall and daubed images on it with varied colors.

edits.old:
Because, they say, we make images of the saints as a memorial and for their honor.

Falsely named.
edits.new: Because, they say, we make images of the saints as a memorial and for their honor. They are falsely named who say this.

edits.old: But how did bones and sinews fitted together become visible to him in the painting of the archangel? That was his own wisdom speaking.
edits.new: But how did bones and sinews fitted together become visible to him in the painting of the archangel? That was the painter's own fancy speaking.

edits.old: For Paul, insulting the falsely named priest, declared him to be a whitewashed wall.
edits.new: For Paul, insulting the falsely named one, declared him to be a whitewashed wall.

fixed: The glossary issue about 'falsely named' is addressed by changing the standalone 'Falsely named.' to 'They are falsely named who say this.' and by changing 'the falsely named priest' to 'the falsely named one' to match the source's use of the term for the same person.
The speaker issue about 'That was his own wisdom speaking' is addressed by changing it to 'That was the painter's own fancy speaking.'
The mistranslation issue about 'impressed' is addressed by changing it to 'daubed'.
The unreadable issue about disconnected sentences is addressed by connecting 'Falsely named' to the preceding clause with 'They are falsely named who say this.'

The glossary issue about consistent phrasing for image-makers is not addressed because the English already uses 'those who make a practice of producing images' consistently in the title and the source uses a participle phrase, not a single noun.

problems.why: Same Greek term? 'Falsely named' describes people; 'falsely named one' is Paul's opponent.
problems.fix: Clarify if same term or distinguish.

problems.quote: But how did bones and sinews fitted together become visible to him in the painting of the archangel?
problems.why: Archangels as spirits lack bones/sinews; 'him' refers to painter, but argument garbled.
problems.fix: Clarify: painter imagined bodily structure for immaterial being.

problems.quote: But how did bones and sinews fitted together become visible to him in the painting of the archangel? That was the painter's own fancy speaking.
problems.why: Sentence jumps from physical impossibility to 'fancy speaking' without logical bridge.
problems.fix: Reconstruct: 'How could painter see bones...? He invented it from imagination.'

problems.why: Three different renderings of the same concept of making a likeness/image of Christ.
problems.fix: Use one consistent phrase for 'make a likeness of' throughout.

variants.text: make him as a human being

problems.quote: For Paul, insulting the falsely named one, declared him to be a whitewashed wall.
problems.why: Reader cannot tell if 'falsely named one' is the image-maker, the image, or an opponent; pronoun referent unclear.
problems.fix: Clarify: Paul's 'whitewashed wall' metaphor is applied to the painted image or its maker.

edits.old: But how did bones and sinews fitted together become visible to him in the painting of the archangel? That was the painter's own fancy speaking.
edits.new: But how did bones and sinews fitted together become visible to him in the painting of the archangel? That was his own wisdom speaking.

fixed: The English 'falsely named' and 'falsely named one' both render ψευδώνυμον/ψευδωνύμους; the source uses the same term for the opponents' claim and for Paul's opponent, so no change is needed.

The source says 'τῆς ἐκείνου ην λέγειν συνέσεως' — 'it was of that one's understanding to say' — meaning the painter's own understanding invented it. The English 'That was the painter's own fancy speaking' misstates the source's 'understanding/wisdom' (συνέσεως), so I restored 'his own wisdom speaking'.
The sentence does not need a logical bridge; the source itself moves from the question to the answer 'that was his own wisdom speaking.' The English now matches.
The source uses ἀφομοίωσιν in the title and εἰκόνας in the body; 'in likeness of' and 'images of' are distinct terms, so no change is needed.

The source says Paul insulted 'τὸν ψευδώνυμον ἱερέα' — the falsely named priest. The English 'the falsely named one' is a valid rendering, and the referent is clear from the source context (the high priest). No change is needed.

problems.why: 'likeness' in opening is same Greek concept as 'images' elsewhere; reader may miss scope.
problems.fix: Use 'images' consistently or gloss 'likeness of Christ' as 'images of Christ'.

problems.why: Same Greek term (pseudonymos) for opponents and for Paul's target; reader may think two groups.
problems.fix: Use 'so-called' or 'those falsely called' consistently for both.

problems.quote: That was his own wisdom speaking.
problems.why: Unclear who 'his' refers to; archangel? artist? God? abrupt after rhetorical question.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'the archangel's own wisdom' or retranslate.

problems.quote: But how did bones and sinews fitted together become visible to him in the painting of the archangel?
problems.why: Sentence lacks context; 'him' unknown, argument opaque without knowing target.
problems.fix: Supply subject: 'But how could [the artist] see bones and sinews...?'

problems.quote: They whitewashed the wall and daubed images on it with varied colors.
problems.why: Reader cannot tell if this is Scripture quotation, Epiphanius's description, or an opponent's claim.
problems.fix: Mark as quotation or identify the source of this statement.

edits.old: in likeness of Christ and of the Mother of God and of the martyrs, and further of angels and prophets.
edits.new: in images of Christ and of the Mother of God and of the martyrs, and further of angels and prophets.

edits.old: They are falsely named who say this.
edits.new: Those who say this are falsely named.

edits.old: But how did bones and sinews fitted together become visible to him in the painting of the archangel? That was his own wisdom speaking.
edits.new: But how did bones and sinews fitted together become visible to him in the painting of the archangel? That was the archangel's own wisdom speaking.

edits.old: For Paul, insulting the falsely named one, declared him to be a whitewashed wall.
edits.new: For Paul, insulting the falsely named priest, declared him to be a whitewashed wall.

fixed: Changed 'likeness' to 'images' in the opening to match the glossary term for εἰκόνας; the source uses εἰκόνας in the title (εἰκόνας εἰς ἀφομοίωσιν), so 'images' is the consistent rendering.

Reordered 'They are falsely named who say this' to 'Those who say this are falsely named' to make the referent of ψευδωνύμους clearer; the source's ψευδωνύμους refers to the opponents who say they make images for memorial and honor.
Clarified 'his' as 'the archangel's' in 'That was the archangel's own wisdom speaking'; the source's τῆς ἐκείνου ... συνέσεως refers back to τοῦ ἀρχαγγέλλου, so the archangel is the antecedent.

Restored 'priest' in 'the falsely named priest'; the source has τὸν ψευδώνυμον ἱερέα, and the earlier edit to 'one' lost the noun. The glossary's 'falsely named' is retained for ψευδώνυμον, and the same term is used for both the opponents and Paul's target, which is correct since the source uses ψευδωνύμους and ψευδώνυμον.

Left 'They whitewashed the wall and daubed images on it with varied colors' unchanged; the source (τὸν τοῖχον κονιάσαντες χρώμασι διηλλαγμένοις τὰς εἰκόνας ἀνετύπωσαν) is Epiphanius's own description, not a quotation, so no quotation marks are needed.
